narrative: Baywood Retail shows a genuine, sustained revenue decline of 26%, spread across nearly every category rather than one culprit. Diagnostic Equipment, its largest line, fell 45% and stayed down for nine months, while smaller lines and eight products also shrank or vanished. Margin, discount and tier mix are all stable, so the leak is pure volume disengagement, not price — and with no seasonal echo or recovery, it looks structural.
cited_evidence: Baywood Retail's monthly revenue fell 26.2%, from a median ₹186,708 to a recent ₹137,753, a statistically significant drop.
Revenue also fell 24% comparing the first half of its history to the second half, confirming a steady decline rather than one bad month.
Diagnostic Equipment, the account's largest category at 19% of spend, dropped 45%, from ₹34,229 to ₹18,765 a month, since August 2025.
Safety Basics and Cleaning & Maintenance each fell roughly 40-45% from smaller bases, and eight separate products lost most or all of their monthly volume, including two that disappeared entirely.
Margin held near 30%, discount stayed flat at about 5%, and high-tier product share edged up slightly, so this is not a pricing or mix problem.
recommended_actions: Contact Baywood Retail to understand why Diagnostic Equipment and other lines have shrunk since mid-2025.
Check whether discontinued products like the Stainless Fastener Pack and Digital Multimeter Pro were lost to a competitor.
Review engagement across all eight categories given the broad-based nature of the decline.

account_level_revenue_impact.basis: Whole-account decline: baseline monthly revenue minus the current monthly rate. Not attributed to any category because no single category explains it.

prioritization.reason: 26.2% of baseline monthly revenue at risk, medium confidence.

churn_risk_projection.basis: Assumes the current monthly loss rate persists unchanged for 12 months — not a forecast of further deterioration, just the cost of inaction at today's rate. Revenue and margin figures overlap and must not be added together.

model_agreement.agent_response: Model leans healthy, but it downplays a statistically significant 26% revenue decline sustained across nearly every category for months.

evidence_timeline.headline: Margin rate is stable
evidence_timeline.method: Erosion threshold: 3.0pp between the baseline and recent windows.

evidence_timeline.headline: Discounting is stable
evidence_timeline.method: Creep threshold: 3.0pp. Discount is revenue-weighted, so a deep discount on a large line counts for more than the same discount on a small one.

evidence_timeline.headline: Product mix is stable
evidence_timeline.detail: High-tier share of revenue 53.1% -> 55.8% (+2.7pp). Low tier 23.9% -> 22.5%.
evidence_timeline.method: Shift threshold: 8.0pp. Direction decides the verdict — the same size of move upward is premiumisation, not a downgrade.

breakdown.note: Lines share the account's expected months of continued buying, so their values add back to the account total. Line losses can exceed the account's value at risk because lines that grew offset part of the loss.

_lifetime_value.note: Lifetime value = value per month x the horizon months (12 or 24), flat. Expected orders and expected active months (BG/NBD, fitted on the whole book) are reported alongside for information and do not scale the money. Baseline uses the value per month before the recent window; current uses the recent window. Value at risk is the gap — the same loss the monthly figures show, on a longer clock. Never add it to monthly revenue at risk.
